current.text: He is Indiana's backup center behind Ivica Zubac and comes off the bench.
The center depth behind him is weak (Larry Nance Jr. or Kobe Brown).
Coach Rick Carlisle keeps center minutes low and runs backups through the rotation. How he splits minutes between Zubac and Huff is an open question.
Expected to play about 10 minutes behind Zubac. He could take all the backup center minutes if he plays well.
Not draftable in standard leagues and not a sleeper. His Yahoo ADP of 102 is too high.
The stash on this team. If Zubac misses time, Huff would have to start.
His 1.9 blocks per game from last season are not expected to hold.
Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, which the expert calls not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: A one category blocks player. Blocks are his only clearly strong category.
Weak in points, rebounds, assists and steals. Steals are a league-level weakness, and his rebounding is low for a center.

note: Huff is a backup center who adds blocks and little else. His 2026-27 projection is 1.4 blocks and 3.0 rebounds per game, and he is weak in steals. Yahoo values him at 0 USD (rank 189) and he went for 1 USD in our league last season, so he should not be drafted in a 144-player auction. Watch early how Carlisle splits minutes between Zubac and Huff, and pick him up if Zubac misses time, since he would then start.
